newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss machinery sector sees foreign orders fall.
newsitem.headline: Swiss machinery sector sees foreign orders fall.

text.p: Swiss machinery makers said foreign orders fell 5.2 percent in the first half of 1996, the first year-on-year drop in five years, as part of an overall decline of 7.1 percent in the period.
The ASM/VSM industry association, which represents Switzerland's biggest export sector, said the strong Swiss franc and weak growth in western Europe had weighed on orders.
"The sector expects orders to stabilise at a low level in the second half of 1996," the group said.

Turnover dipped 3.7 percent in the first half compared with the same period in 1995. Capacity utilisation slipped to 86.6 percent at the end of June from 88.3 percent in March and 88.5 percent at the end of 1995.

Exports rose 3.0 percent to 21,478 million francs thanks to good foreign demand until the end of last year. Exports to western Europe stagnated, but sales to some Asian countries jumped. Exports to Indonesia rose 66.3 percent, to Singapore 46.5 percent, to India 34.1 percent and to Japan 23.5 percent.
Exports to the United States, the second-biggest market after Germany, rose 3.5 percent in the half.
The group appealed to the government to help it gain access to European markets by concluding a deal with the European Union on trade ties.
"A breakthrough in the bilateral negotiations with the EU could contribute to reducing the uncertainty in the machinery industry," it said.
